title: Cache coordination: lease-based proposal review (synthesis & open items)
agenda: Proposal walkthrough: lease coordinator and short-lived leases
summary: This session reviewed the lease-based cache coordination proposal intended to reduce coherent cache thrash across multi-tenant serving clusters. We validated core invariants, surfaced a small set of failure modes, and agreed on a minimal implementation plus experiments before full rollout.
discussion_notes:
Background: We continue to see cross-tenant cache churn when many warm sessions start KV-prefetch concurrently. The proposed approach is to introduce short-lived (100-500ms) leader leases for a cache key prefix shard to serialize prefetch + writeback decisions and reduce duplicated work.

Proposal walkthrough: Lena presented the coordinator service sketch: per-node local lease manager + optional global lease arbiter for cross-rack coordination. Leases are optimistic, renewal-based. When a node wins a lease for prefix P it may perform prefetch and mark KV entries hot; other nodes observing the lease will treat ongoing fills as in-progress and wait or attach to the existing inflight promise.

Failure and partition semantics: We enumerated cases: coordinator crash, network partition (split-brain), slow renewals, lease starvation, and lease-holder slow-path. Key reasoning: safety requires only one writer of hot-prefetch side-effects at a time; availability should prefer degraded read-through rather than blocking inference. The team proposed strong correctness: leases are the only mechanism that gates background prefetch writes; inference read paths remain lock-free (reads fall back to direct fetch).

Leases vs leader election: We explicitly prefer time-bounded leases over leader election because leases are simpler to revoke and compose with opportunistic writebacks. We noted that a global Paxos-style leader is overkill for per-prefix coordination and increases blast radius.

Multi-tenant & capacity concerns: Ravi called out scenario where a single noisy tenant could hoard lease slots for large ranges of keys. Mitigations discussed: per-tenant lease quotas, lease weighting by tenant QPS, and aging heuristics. We also noted CPU and RPC overhead for lease renewals at high QPS and flagged batching renewals as a later optimization.

Metrics and observability: Required telemetry includes lease acquisition latency, lease renewal rate, number of concurrent inflight fills per prefix, per-tenant lease hold time distribution, and failure counts (renewal failures, coordinator timeouts). We will add tracing hooks to connect inference request traces to lease events to understand user-visible latencies.

Test and verification: Unit tests for lease invariants, integration test harness that injects partitions and coordinator crashes, and a canary in a low-throughput zone for two weeks with synthetic warmup traffic. We’ll collect divergence metrics comparing prefetch success rate and end-to-end token latency relative to baseline.

Rollout strategy: Start with node-local lease manager only (no cross-rack arbiter) in canary. If safe, enable optional coordinator for intra-region coordination behind a feature flag. Rollback plan is to disable lease checking so prefetch falls back to the previous best-effort approach.

Open items and tradeoffs discussed:
- Lease timeout tuning: 100–300ms seemed reasonable; we will try 150ms default in canary.
- Lease renewal backpressure: renewals must be piggybacked on existing control path to avoid RPC storms.
- Hot-prefix detection: threshold for creating leases vs letting reads continue without coordination.
- Data-path coupling: ensure that lease logic is orthogonal to the kernel selection path to avoid broad coupling of runtime components.
- Compaction and eviction interactions: need to ensure lease holders do not prevent timely eviction for memory pressure scenarios.

Takeaways: The design is promising and low-risk if we start with local leases and conservative timeouts. The team wants concrete experiments to quantify reduced duplicate prefetches and overall CPU/RPC overhead before enabling cross-rack coordination.
decisions: Implement node-local short-lived lease manager as the first tranche
Default lease timeout set to 150ms for canary runs
Inference reads remain lock-free and read-through on miss (no blocking on lease)
Per-tenant lease quota to be introduced before enabling cross-rack coordinator
Feature-flag gated cross-rack coordinator: disabled by default
